chose: keep classify.ts's own strict {{recipe_json}} substitution rather than calling Prompts.compile()

because: compile() documents that unmatched variables are LEFT UNCHANGED, so a prompt edited in PostHog to reference a variable the pipeline does not supply would silently send a literal {{foo}} to the model. classify.ts's version throws instead, which turns that editing mistake into a failed job with a message rather than a corpus of quietly-degraded labels. Revisit if the strictness ever blocks a legitimate prompt edit

chose: run-once becomes a pure job trigger: it enqueues and exits, assuming a running server and worker
over: keeping consoleHost's in-process graph execution so the CLI works with no stack up
because: consoleHost was a second execution engine — it re-implemented fan-out, child-failure folding and concurrency in-process, so the code path a developer iterated on was NOT the code path production ran, and its failure modes were shared with nothing. Trading 'works with no stack' for 'one execution engine, and the job is visible in Bull Board' is what the user asked for and is the honest trade

chose: merge counts ride a separate llm_enrichment_completed event keyed by the same $ai_trace_id; pre-call facts ride the span
over: dropping labels_written/disagreements entirely
delaying the span until after the merge so everything fits on it
because: enrichSpan fires at span CREATION and labels_written/disagreements only exist after generateText returns and mergeLlmLabels runs — there is no hook late enough. line_count/unresolved_line_count ARE known pre-call so they stay on the span. chose: a schema rejection emits llm_enrichment_failed, not a second $ai_generation
over: keeping the old behaviour of one $ai_generation with $ai_is_error for ANY throw
because: the two failure classes are genuinely different and the native path tells them apart: a transport failure happens inside doGenerate so the SDK's own span records the error for free, while a schema rejection happens ABOVE the model layer — doGenerate succeeded, tokens were spent, only the parse failed — so the generation span records a success, which is what it was. That retires the $ai_is_error signal any dashboard was reading, so the domain event carries it instead with the same trace id, the message and the model's raw text. Emitting a second $ai_generation would have preserved the signal at the cost of double-counting one model call in cost and volume

chose: BasicTracerProvider + trace.setGlobalTracerProvider, registered from a Fastify plugin
over: NodeSDK, which the plan specified
a side-effecting import at the top of each entrypoint, or a node --import loader flag
because: NodeSDK produced recording spans and exported NONE of them with a caller-supplied spanProcessors array (dual-package hazard checked and refuted first); BasicTracerProvider with the identical processor exported immediately, and drops @opentelemetry/sdk-node's auto-instrumentation/metrics/logs stack this service never wanted. A plugin rather than an entrypoint import because generateText runs inside a BullMQ job, long after buildApp() — the provider only has to exist before the first SPAN, not the first import, which buys one shutdown path through onClose and no launch command to keep in sync across Railway, process-compose and package.json
